newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady ahead of CPI.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady ahead of CPI.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were quietly steady in moderate trade, dealers said on Thursday.
Most traders were sidelined ahead of tonight's release of the U.S. April consumer price index (CPI), weekly jobless claims and April industrial production/capacity utilisation data.
The consumer price index for April, is forecast to be unchanged from the 0.1 percent gain reported in March.
Weekly jobless claims for the week ended May 10, are forecast to be around 340,000 compared with the previous week's 347,000.
Industrial production for April are expected to show a gain of 0.2 percent from a 0.9 percent increase in March. April capacity utilisation is expected to be unchanged from March's 84.1 percent.

"Rates were steady to slightly higher in the morning on some position adjustments. Some people are waiting for fresh clues to market direction from tonight's release of the consumer price index, weekly jobless claims, industrial production and capacity utilisation data," a local dealer said.
"But unless the numbers are way off market expectations, I don't think there will be much impact," he said.
In day-to-day rates, Thursday/Friday rose 3/16 percentage point to 5-3/4 5-5/8 percent, weekend rose 1/8 point to 5-11/16 5-9/16 percent and week-fixed rose 1/16 point to 5-11/16 5-9/16 percent.

Among longer dates, two-months was unchanged from Wednesday's 5-3/4 5-5/8 percent, four-months unchanged at 5-13/16 5-11/16, six-months unchanged at 6 5-7/8 and twelve-months unchanged at 6-1/4 6-1/9 percent.
